findings.title: `float: right` on small-action button is ignored once the container is flex
findings.body: `.small-action` is now a flex container (lines 264-265), and floats have no effect on flex items. The `button { float: right; }` rule therefore no longer pushes the action button to the right edge. `.small-action-desc` has no `flex-grow`, so the button now sits directly after the description text instead of right-aligned. Give the button `margin-left: auto`, or let the description grow (e.g. `flex: 1`). The same applies to the now-dead `float: left` on `.topic-avatar`.

findings.title: align-items mixin emits a bogus property and passes modern values to legacy syntaxes
findings.body: `-ms-align-items` does not exist, so it is dead output. `-webkit-box-align` and `-ms-flex-align` only accept `start`/`end`/`center`/`baseline`/`stretch`, but the mixin passes `$alignment` through unchanged. Calls like `align-items(flex-start)` or `align-items(flex-end)` would produce invalid declarations for those engines. The mixin also omits `-moz-box-align`, even though the flexbox mixins emit `display: -moz-box`. Old Firefox would get a box layout with default (stretch) alignment rather than the requested one.

findings.title: order mixin maps `order` directly onto 1-based box-ordinal-group
findings.body: `-webkit-box-ordinal-group` and `-moz-box-ordinal-group` are 1-based and must be positive integers, with a default of 1. Modern `order` defaults to 0 and accepts 0 and negative values. Passing `$val` straight through means `order(0)` or `order(-1)` would be invalid in the legacy syntax. Items with `order(1)` would also be indistinguishable from unordered items there. The usual approach is to emit `$val + 1` for the box-ordinal-group properties.

findings.title: `margin-left: auto` right-alignment does not work in the legacy -webkit-box/-moz-box fallback
findings.body: The panel used to be right-aligned with `float: right`; it is now pushed right with `margin-left: auto` inside the flex `.contents`. The 2009 box model emitted first by the flexbox mixin (`display: -webkit-box` / `-moz-box`) does not distribute auto margins. Browsers that only understand that syntax, which are the reason those prefixes were added, would render the panel immediately after the title rather than at the right edge.
